This is going to be long. I hope this is the right place for it and it won't get downvoted. I got here from /r/all and I saw someone ask "what is the alt-right?". I have refrained from posting about politics this election cycle but I want to share this story with anyone who will listen.

Remember Gamergate? For those who don't know what it is, the extreme tldr of the story is that a female game developer traded sex with a games journalist for favourable coverage. From there ensued a bunch more drama involving many female figures in the games industry. (Do your own research if you want more than that; it's too controversial for me to give unbiased details)

I'm a game dev and I'm involved in games media. I was super involved with Gamergate, back when it was actually about "ethics in games journalism". And for a short time, it was. There were a lot of genuine, ethical issues at play there.

This is how I was seduced.

A cause I identified with, felt involved with. I knew I was on the right side (and I still believe I was). I had the facts; I was in the industry and I knew the kind of shit that was going on. This gave me a blind spot.

The subreddit I frequented, KotakuInAction, was bombarded with article after article about the various controversies involving the people at the center of Gamergate. At first, most of them were very legitimate! It was non-partisan at the time. We were pissed off: Censorship, abuses of power, cries of harrassment at the first sign of drama. This wasn't "the right" vs. "the left", it was gamers against censorship.

So how did that evolve? Well, an "opposing side" was created (GamerGhazi). That opposing side found its own cause: social justice. Women were being targeted for harrassment, that needed to stop. That's how "ethics in games journalism" started fighting "protecting women against harrassment".

Both sides originally had a legitimate, worthy cause, but GamerGate was no longer fighting for ethics, it was now fighting against the people involved. It starts by cherry-picking the bottom of the barrel, the cases where "the other side" is clearly wrong. Mistakes happen on both sides. And as with any subreddit rising in popularity, clickbait takes over. People don't do research, don't fact-check, so "fake news" (at the time we called it "bullshit") falls through the crack. Made up stories, only there to demonize the other side.

It keeps going for weeks. Months. It's a vicious circle: the more time you spend reading those stories, the more you demonize your opponent until they're LITERALLY HITLER. It's very, very fucking hard to convince anyone, on either side, that they're wrong about it because there's weeks and weeks of cherry-picked crap and propaganda backing up their beliefs.

This was me. I try really, really fucking hard to be a good person in my life and I thought I was still with the Good Guys. I hadn't noticed that half of the crap on the subreddit was now originating from very few sources, all of which stood to profit from a group of internet warriors pissed off at another group of internet warriors.

I want you to understand this: This was happening on both sides. Both sides were being radicalized with made-up crap about the other. Both sides harrassed the other. Both sides were shit. And yet, the majority of the people on both sides were just good-hearted, selfless people who found a cause to believe in. We'd all been duped.

I stopped posting when the subreddit was no longer about games at all. (I had a quick look at it right now, it still isn't - there's a grand total of one post out of 20 that's remotely related to video games. Same for the other one.) But I still followed very closely. I was very angry at the injustice and how "the other side" had obviously been duped, without realizing that so had I. I sought to understand; so I talked to some "SJWs"... listened to them, all of them had such terrible ideas about what this was about. How could they be so wrong, so naive?

I eventually figured this was no longer worth my time. I left. I didn't think much of it afterwards... until Trump was elected and I had a very close look at the alt-right and realized the connection to gamergate. This is when I connected the dots. Holy shit, was I really in that group?

Today, I cannot picture myself ever voting for somebody like Trump. And yet, were I a US citizen, I fully believe I would have if I hadn't left Gamergate when I did. I still wonder, how could I have been so stupid? I was part of a cult. I know cults and I know brainwashing, I have researched them extensively, you'd think I would have noticed, right? Wrong. These are the same tactics that Scientology and ISIS use and I fell for them like a chump.

This is my story. I want to leave you with this: Whenever you hear stories about how evil the other side is, they're probably either wrong or cherry-picked. Brainwashing doesn't only happen in the alt-right, it happens here too. Be on your guard, give people the benefit of the doubt and above all, don't answer hate with hate.

And if you, dear reader, are an alt-righter and got this far into my post for some reason, you need to hear this too: Take a good, long look around you. I know it looks bad out here, but trust me, it's far worse where you are. The people you think are corrupt, shills, pro-censorship, self-serving or just plain evil, most of them aren't. Some of them are! You can still avoid those! But I beg you, if you do not identify with the "neo-nazi" label, you need to reconsider what you are doing with your life.

Peace.
